name: Blackened Chicken with Mango Salsa
writer_notes: Olive oil is a DIVIDED buy (7 tbsp): I split it in prose, roughly 3 1/2 tbsp into the salsa and the remainder into the skillet, so the full purchased quantity is used across two steps.

The source transcription lists a 12th ingredient, Primal Kitchen Avocado Lime Dipping Sauce, as an optional 'if using' garnish. It is NOT in the 11 locked buy lines, so I deliberately kept it out of the method and shop_smart and added it to forbidden_prose_terms - no step may use an ingredient nobody purchased. If the intent is to sell it, it needs a buy line added upstream; I left the recipe as shopped.
All 11 locked ingredients are used by a step; no step uses anything off the buy list.
Macros used in prose (620 cal, 43.6 g protein, 61.9 g carbs, 22.2 g fat) are verbatim from the locked view and satisfy this run's band (450-800 cal, protein >= 40).
No cost_lines were provided in this dispatch, so shop_smart makes no per-ounce or per-package cost claims; cost appears only as the ${{cost_ps}} token plus the $1/month membership line.
Scaling from the source (~3.5x) is internally consistent and quantities are plausible for 14 servings; no data flags.

prose.intro_html:
Blackened chicken with mango salsa is the kind of dinner that looks like a twenty dollar patio plate and actually costs you a rounding error. Spice-crusted chicken breast, a fresh salsa of mango, avocado, cilantro and red onion, all sitting on a bed of cilantro lime rice. Fourteen containers out of one cook.

The numbers do the talking. Every serving lands at 620 calories with 43.6 grams of protein, 61.9 grams of carbs and 22.2 grams of fat, and it comes in at ${{cost_ps}} a serving. Sweet mango against smoky blackening seasoning is a combination that keeps you eating clean because it never tastes like eating clean.
prose.shop_smart:
Here is how to shop this one without overthinking it.

  • You need 3 1/2 large mangoes, ripe but not mushy. A ripe mango gives a little when you press near the stem and smells sweet at that end. If the store only has hard ones, buy a few days early and let them sit on the counter.
  • Grab 3 1/2 large avocados. Buy them at a mix of ripeness so they are not all rock hard on cook day. They get diced into the salsa, so slightly firm beats overripe.
  • The rice is the shortcut: seven 10 oz bags of frozen cilantro lime rice, about 14 cups prepared. Frozen packets cook in minutes and keep the labor down on a 14-serving batch.
  • Chicken breast is the anchor at 5 1/4 lb, so reach for the big family pack of boneless skinless breast.
  • You need 3 1/2 bunches of fresh cilantro, about 7 oz, and a couple of red onions for the 1 1/4 cups minced. Round up on cilantro, it wilts fast and you would rather have extra.
prose.make_it:
Start with the salsa so the flavors can mingle while you cook. Dice 3 1/2 large mangoes, dice 3 1/2 large avocados, chop your 3 1/2 bunches of cilantro and mince the red onion down to about 1 1/4 cups. Pile it all into a big bowl.

Season the salsa with salt and pepper to taste, then add about 3 1/2 tablespoons of the olive oil and the 3 1/2 tablespoons of fresh lime juice. That oil is divided, so hold the rest back for the skillet. Toss until it is well combined and set it aside.

Now the chicken. Dice 5 1/4 lb of boneless skinless chicken breast into 1 inch cubes. Add the 6 tablespoons of blackened seasoning and toss until every piece is coated.

Heat the rest of your olive oil in a large cast iron skillet over medium-high heat. Work in batches so you do not crowd the pan, and cook the chicken about 3 minutes per side until it is no longer pink in the center and reaches an internal temperature of 165 F. Then let it rest.

Cook the frozen cilantro lime rice, all seven 10 oz bags, right on the package instructions. That comes out to about 14 cups prepared.

Assemble: a bed of cilantro lime rice, blackened chicken on top, and a good spoon of mango salsa to finish. Sit down at the table and enjoy it.
prose.portion_html:
Fourteen containers, and the honest way to split them even is to weigh, not eyeball. Zero out your scale under an empty container, weigh the full pot of rice and divide by 14 so every box gets the same base. Do the same with the chicken. The salsa goes on last, a heaping spoon per box, or keep it in small side cups if you are storing these more than a day or two so the avocado stays fresh.

Each container comes out to 620 calories, 43.6 grams of protein, 61.9 grams of carbs and 22.2 grams of fat. That is your dinner sorted for two weeks of workdays.
prose.cost_closing_html: This is the whole point of cooking in bulk. Blackened chicken with mango salsa over cilantro lime rice runs ${{cost_ps}} a serving, and you built fourteen of them in one session. Set that next to a single fast-casual bowl and the math is not close.

head.description: Meal prep blackened chicken with fresh mango salsa over cilantro lime rice. Fourteen high-protein servings at 620 calories and 43.6 g protein each, built for a budget.
head.keywords: blackened chicken, mango salsa, meal prep, high protein dinner, cilantro lime rice, budget meal prep, chicken breast, 14 servings
steps: Make the mango salsa: dice the mangoes and avocados, chop the cilantro, and mince the red onion into a large bowl. Season with salt and pepper, add part of the divided olive oil and the fresh lime juice, and toss to combine. Set aside.
Dice the chicken breast into 1 inch cubes and toss with the blackened seasoning until every piece is coated.

Heat the remaining olive oil in a large cast iron skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken in batches about 3 minutes per side until no longer pink in the center and at 165 F internal, then let it rest.
Cook the frozen cilantro lime rice according to the package instructions.
Assemble each bowl: cilantro lime rice on the bottom, blackened chicken on top, and mango salsa to finish.
